items.title: XRP Ledger Discloses Flaw That Could Create Unauthorized XRP...Emergency Patch Deployed Without Amendment Vote
items.content:
XRP Ledger (XRPL) developers disclosed on October 9 fixes for two vulnerabilities. The central issue was a payment-processing error confirmed in a separate test environment that could allow XRP to be created improperly and then spent. Developers estimated that the flaw had existed since 2015 and said they found no evidence that it had been exploited on any public network.
The error occurred when amounts from multiple offers were added: if the calculation exceeded its limit, the total wrapped around to a small number. An attacker could exploit this to pay more XRP to recipient accounts than was deducted from the buyer's account. Developers reproduced the behavior on a test server and explained that the safeguard designed to prevent the creation of new XRP failed to catch it because it used the same faulty calculation.
The fix was included in xrpld 3.4.1, released on September 25. Changes to transaction-processing rules normally require support from more than 80% of trusted validators to be maintained for two weeks under the amendment process. This payment-error fix, however, took effect as soon as a server was upgraded. The report said this was the first time since the amendment system was introduced that a transaction-processing change had deliberately been deployed this way. Members of the XRPL Foundation, RippleX and the validator community judged that the risk of exploitation if the fix were disclosed while awaiting a vote outweighed the risk that differing server behavior during the emergency rollout could halt consensus. More than 80% of validators on the default Unique Node List (UNL) upgraded on the day of release.
Meanwhile, the Batch transaction validation error disclosed at the same time affected a feature that was not active on Mainnet when it was discovered, so it did not affect Mainnet accounts or funds. That fix went through the normal amendment process and was activated on October 9. The report said the standard process for rules changes remains in place and did not present a standing exception-approval procedure for similar future cases.
items.metanomia_thought: This incident shows that trust in a blockchain depends both on code safety and validators' ability to respond to crises. XRPL skipped the amendment vote and waiting period and applied an emergency patch for the unauthorized-minting vulnerability through rapid validator upgrades. There is tension between procedures that give decentralized consensus time and the need for rapid crisis response; in this case, part of the established process was set aside to gain speed.

items.title: Thailand's SEC Finalizes Bitcoin and Ether ETF Rules...Effective October 16
items.content:
Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced 11 notifications on October 8 governing the establishment and operation of crypto-asset exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The rules take effect on October 16, and the initial eligible assets are Bitcoin and Ether.
An ETF must be managed as a passive fund tracking the price of one crypto asset. Its average net exposure to that crypto asset over each accounting year must remain at least 80% of net asset value (NAV). Crypto-asset ETFs in Thailand may be listed and traded only on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET). Before trading, investors must confirm that they understand the product's features and risks, and securities companies may not provide margin loans to finance ETF purchases. Crypto assets must be held by a licensed digital-asset custodian supervised by Thailand's SEC.
Asset managers may outsource digital-asset management only to licensed digital-asset fund managers. Digital-asset businesses such as custodians may apply to register as mutual fund supervisors for crypto-asset ETFs if they meet financial, staffing and operational-system requirements. Even if the mutual fund supervisor appoints a separate sub-custodian, the crypto assets must be held by a licensed custodian.
Mutual funds and private funds that were already allowed to invest in overseas crypto-asset ETFs will also be able to invest in Thai ETFs within their existing investment limits. At the initial stage, however, alternative products such as depositary receipts (DRs) referencing overseas crypto-asset ETFs will not be permitted. Securities companies also may not intermediate overseas crypto-asset ETF investments for clients other than institutional investors and ultra-high-net-worth investors.
October 16 is the effective date of the rules; the announcement did not specify when the first ETF would be listed or which asset managers would participate.
items.metanomia_thought: Thailand is channeling demand for crypto-asset investment into a financial market involving domestic asset managers, exchanges and custodians. If South Korea also establishes a domestic listing route and management and custody standards for spot ETFs, it may become easier to track the scale and flow of funds entering such products within the domestic supervisory framework. Allowing domestic ETFs would open new business opportunities for financial firms while directing investment demand into a market subject to disclosure and supervision.

items.title: U.S. CFTC Proposes Explicitly Treating Sports and Political Event Contracts as Swaps...Sportsbook Bets and Casino Games Excluded
items.content:
The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) released a proposed rule on October 9 local time that would expressly include event contracts in the definition of a swap. It would cover contracts based on sports, political, cultural and weather-related events, among others.
The CFTC said these contracts are financial products commonly known in the industry as swaps and that the proposal is intended to resolve uncertainty over their classification. Chairman Michael Selig said event contracts are commodity derivatives under the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) and fall within the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction. The comment period will run for 30 days from publication of the proposal in the Federal Register.
The same day, the CFTC also announced an interim final rule codifying its existing position that casino-style gambling products, including bets placed through sportsbooks and casino games, are not swaps. Selig said casino-style gambling products are not derivatives and described the rule as a step to clarify the limits of the CFTC's regulatory remit. The rule takes effect immediately upon publication in the Federal Register, with comments accepted for 30 days after publication.
The announcements did not resolve the jurisdictional dispute with state gambling laws. Litigation continues over whether state gambling laws may be applied to sports event contracts offered by prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket. CoinDesk reported that federal appellate rulings were divided, with one favoring the CFTC's position and two favoring the states.
The proposal to expressly include event contracts in the swap definition remains at the proposal stage, and the announcements did not specify whether it will be finally adopted or when it would take effect.
items.metanomia_thought: Prediction markets can develop into financial markets that place prices on future uncertainty, aggregate information and trade risk. The CFTC's proposal can be read as an effort to bring this demand within derivatives regulation and create a foundation for new products and businesses to grow. If South Korea broadens the path for experimenting with on-chain finance within the regulated sector, it could expand opportunities for domestic financial companies to participate in price formation, settlement and trading revenue around domestic assets and events.

items.title: ESMA Calls for Halt to Custody and Transfers of Stablecoins That Fail MiCA Requirements…Three-Month Wind-Down Deadline
items.content:
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) issued a supervisory opinion on October 8 calling for services related to stablecoins that do not meet the requirements of the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) to be discontinued. It covers asset-referenced tokens (ARTs) and e-money tokens (EMTs) that do not meet the requirements for lawful public offering or admission to trading in the EU.
ESMA said crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) authorized under MiCA must not provide EU clients with related services including trading, exchange, execution of orders, custody, transfer and advice. The opinion sets supervisory expectations for national competent authorities (NCAs) to apply existing MiCA obligations consistently.
In a January 2025 statement, ESMA had said that custody and transfer alone could continue. The new opinion brings those services within supervisory expectations and states that regulators may temporarily allow only services necessary to wind down existing holdings. It concluded that risk warnings or disclosures by service providers cannot substitute for the redemption rights, reserve assets and asset-protection safeguards required at issuance.
ESMA said national regulators should require remaining holdings and related services to be wound down as soon as possible and no later than three months from the publication of the opinion. Sales, conversions, withdrawals, transfers and custody needed to prevent customer harm may qualify for temporary exceptions, but new purchases, promotions and ongoing trading services do not fall within that scope.
The opinion did not identify specific tokens. CoinDesk cited USDT and PYUSD as examples and calculated the three-month deadline as January 8, 2027. The materials did not provide country-specific implementation schedules or service termination dates for individual providers.
items.metanomia_thought: The United States sees stablecoin regulation as a means of extending the dollar’s international influence. By contrast, ESMA’s opinion calls for winding down even the trading, custody and transfer channels for tokens that fail MiCA requirements. The competitiveness of dollar stablecoins therefore depends not only on scale and liquidity, but also on whether they can comply with both U.S. and European rules and connect the two markets.

items.title: Samsung Wallet Plans Late-October USDC Transfers in the U.S.…Bank Transfers to More Than 60 Countries
items.content:
Samsung Electronics America announced on October 7 that it will begin offering stablecoin wallet features in Samsung Wallet to U.S. Galaxy users in the final week of October. The first supported asset will be USDC, a U.S. dollar-linked stablecoin. Eligible users are U.S. residents aged 18 or older with a Samsung account and a compatible Galaxy device running Android 13 or later. Account enrollment, identity verification and biometric authentication setup are required. Samsung said there are 82 million Samsung Wallet-compatible Galaxy devices in the United States.
Users will be able to send USDC to external wallets and exchange accounts on supported networks. Samsung will not charge a fee for these transfers, although the receiving provider may charge one. Users will also be able to send funds to supported bank accounts in more than 60 countries, with recipients receiving local currency. Bank transfer fees vary by country and amount, and the app will display the fee and estimated arrival time before the transfer is confirmed.
Regulated partners will provide account, custody and transfer services, with Bastion supplying the related infrastructure. Coinbase is Bastion’s official sub-custodian and will hold Samsung Wallet’s USDC in Coinbase Prime Vault. Solana and Sui are among the network support partners.
Samsung said it is not a bank, money transmitter or digital-asset custodian and does not hold customer funds. Use of the service is subject to partner terms. Online and in-store payments and expansion to additional countries were presented as possible future features. The announcement did not provide a specific list of countries supported for international bank transfers or the applicable fee rates.
items.metanomia_thought: Samsung is securing the customer interface for stablecoin use without holding customer funds directly. Bastion and Coinbase provide the financial infrastructure, while Samsung connects users through its existing app and devices. The competition to expand stablecoin adoption is moving beyond token issuance to the question of who controls the everyday transfer screen.

items.title: Securitize Announces Tokenized Products for 12 U.S. Stocks Including Apple and Nvidia…USDC Settlement on Solana
items.content:
Tokenization platform Securitize announced on October 8 U.S. Eastern Time the launch of ‘Securitize Stocks,’ which enables trading of U.S. equities on a blockchain. The initial lineup consists of 12 names: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Tesla, Meta, Amazon, Netflix, Circle, SpaceX, Strategy and Palantir.
Each token is backed one-to-one by actual shares and represents a security entitlement under Article 8 of the U.S. Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). The structure is designed to preserve dividends, voting rights and other rights attached to the shares. Holders own their rights through the broker-dealer Securitize Markets and are not registered shareholders entered directly on the issuing company’s shareholder register.
If an issuing company adopts tokenization with direct participation and conversion is offered, holders may convert their positions through a transfer agent into shares recorded on the company’s shareholder register. Securitize said it will not lend the underlying shares and that the companies issuing those shares have not sponsored or officially endorsed the product.
Trading will take place through Securitize’s proprietary automated market maker, PropAMM, on Solana, with Jump Trading serving as market maker. Settlement will use USDC. The service will initially operate during extended trading hours and is planned to expand to 24-hour, year-round trading. It is available to investors in permitted jurisdictions, including the United States and the EU, who meet local legal and eligibility requirements and complete know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering (AML) procedures.
Securitize also plans to pursue trading on the digital venue being developed by the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and on the tokenized securities market of OKXICE, a joint venture between ICE and OKX. Neither venue has launched, and trading may not materialize depending on regulatory approval and venue review. The announcement did not provide fees or minimum trade sizes.
items.metanomia_thought: Securitize is combining stock brokerage with an automated market maker and stablecoin settlement, crossing the operating boundary between securities firms and crypto-asset platforms. Shareholder rights remain within the existing securities system, but the customer interface and the technology that processes trades move onchain. Traditional financial licenses remain necessary, yet the assumption that incumbent financial firms will continue to control both customer access and trading revenue is becoming less secure.

items.title: Coinbase Completes Deribit Integration…Plans to Link U.S. and International Derivatives Liquidity
items.content:
Coinbase said on October 7 that it had completed the integration of Deribit and established the ‘Coinbase Global Exchange.’ The company plans to connect U.S. and international derivatives liquidity and roll out options, spot margin and unified portfolio features in stages.
U.S. institutional clients will access Deribit options and perpetual futures on Coinbase Prime through Coinbase Financial Markets (CFM), a futures commission merchant. Prime options trading will become available within weeks, and onboarding has begun. Options trading for eligible users outside the United States is also planned within weeks, while options trading for U.S. retail customers is scheduled for later this year.
In May, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Market Participants Division said certain Deribit perpetual contracts could be treated as foreign futures. It also issued conditional no-action relief for a structure in which customer crypto-asset collateral is held with Coinbase Bermuda (CBBM) and reused for that customer’s foreign futures and options trading. Any reuse must be based on the customer agreement and local regulations. According to the letter, if position liquidations and Deribit’s insurance fund are insufficient to cover a shortfall, Deribit may proportionally reduce the settlement profits of members who made gains during the previous 24-hour settlement cycle.
The unified portfolio feature accounts for offsetting positions to reduce required margin. Spot margin offers leverage of up to 10 times on certain major assets and up to five times on other supported assets, and in the United States it is available only to eligible contract participants (ECPs). In supported regions, global derivatives are offered by CBBM, which is regulated by the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA). Spot margin is a product of a separate affiliate and is not offered by CFM.
Coinbase Pro is scheduled to relaunch by year-end as a professional platform supporting spot, futures, perpetual futures, options and equity trading. The announcement did not provide specific launch dates for the new features.
items.metanomia_thought: Coinbase aims to bring customers’ trading activity and collateral onto its platform by combining Deribit’s options liquidity with margin management. For offshore trading through CFM, collateral may be reused under the relevant agreements and regulations, and Deribit members’ settlement profits may be reduced if liquidations and the insurance fund fail to cover a shortfall. Customers gain the convenience of lower margin requirements, but the security of collateral management and settlement also depends on the operations of overseas affiliates and the exchange.

items.title: Moody’s Assigns B3 Rating to USDS Operator Sky Protocol…Outlook Stable
items.content:
Sky Frontier Foundation announced on October 7 local time that Moody’s Ratings had assigned Sky Protocol a B3 issuer rating with a stable outlook. The foundation said this was the first time Moody’s had rated a stablecoin protocol. B3 is a speculative-grade rating below investment grade and indicates high credit risk.
Sky is an onchain financial protocol that issues the U.S. dollar stablecoin USDS. Independent capital allocators receive USDS liquidity and invest it across several strategies within risk limits set by governance, with the resulting returns flowing into protocol revenue.
The foundation said Moody’s viewed the level of ‘Sky Reserves’ as a major rating factor. Sky governance has shifted to a framework that retains part of the protocol’s net income until reserves reach a minimum target, and the foundation said building those reserves will take time. S&P Global Ratings has described the protocol’s surplus reserves as capital available to absorb credit losses that could arise from its assets.
S&P previously assigned Sky Protocol a B- rating with a stable outlook on August 7, 2025. That assessment cited depositor concentration, centralized governance and capital that was insufficient relative to the risk of the assets as key constraints. S&P assessed the creditworthiness of USDS and DAI as well as the savings tokens sUSDS and sDAI, defining a reduction in the redemption amount owed to token holders as a default.
The foundation said it will review the upgrade factors identified by both rating agencies with Sky governance and announce an implementation plan, with investment grade as the long-term goal. It also said that it is an independent organization that does not control the protocol or DAO governance. The announcement did not state when the reserve target would be reached.
items.metanomia_thought: Sky presents obtaining credit ratings as part of its reserve-building strategy and names investment grade as its long-term goal. The more of the same earnings it distributes as rewards, the less it retains as reserves to absorb losses. Just as a bank retains earnings to strengthen capital, Sky is using part of the income it could distribute today to invest in future credit quality and growth.

items.title: Tether Signs Agreement with Kazakhstan’s Central Bank…Plans Tenge-Linked Stablecoin Pilot Proposal
items.content:
Stablecoin issuer Tether announced on October 7 that it had signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the National Bank of Kazakhstan (NBK) and the Alatau City Authority (ACA). The three organizations plan to jointly study potential uses for stablecoin development, asset tokenization and decentralized finance (DeFi).
The agreement includes studying international stablecoin issuance models and use cases, and preparing a concept and pilot proposal for a stablecoin linked to Kazakhstan’s currency, the tenge.
The parties will also work on a framework for asset tokenization. They plan to select the asset classes to be tokenized first, design a conceptual model and pursue a pilot in Alatau, where a special legal framework applies. They will also consider using Tether’s Hadron tokenization platform, but its adoption has not been decided.
Training will be provided to central bank and other government personnel on stablecoin issuance and reserve-management models and the tokenization of real-world assets. Binur Zhalenov, deputy governor of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, said maintaining financial stability, transaction transparency and investor protection would remain the top priority while studying international examples.
CoinDesk described the agreement as exploratory and said it was not a decision to issue a tenge-linked stablecoin. The announcement did not identify the issuer, reserve structure or a specific implementation timetable.
items.metanomia_thought: The agreement shows Tether seeking to apply its stablecoin issuance experience to the digitization of a local currency and other assets. If Hadron is selected for the tokenization pilot, Tether could participate both in researching the issuance model and in providing the underlying technology. Its experience issuing USDT would then become an asset in a technical partnership to help government and local authorities design digital-finance infrastructure.

items.title: Abstract Announces Ethereum L2 Shutdown…Users Told to Move Assets Before December 15
items.content:
Ethereum layer-2 (L2) blockchain Abstract announced a plan on October 6 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to wind down operations. The chain, which has been backed by Igloo, the operator of NFT project Pudgy Penguins, is scheduled to cease operations on December 15, 2026.
The operators said Abstract had attracted more than 144 apps and over 400,000 users. However, they said that stagnant growth, insufficient liquidity, a limited decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem and low institutional participation meant that independently operating a chain focused on consumer crypto-asset services was not sustainable.
Igloo CEO Luca Netz said the company had lost tens of millions of dollars while supporting Abstract over the past 18 months. It decided not to issue a new token to keep the chain running and plans to focus its resources on Pudgy Penguins and PENGU-related businesses.
Ethereum L2 Blast had also announced a shutdown on October 2. Blast said the cost of maintaining the chain exceeded its revenue and that it had found no clear path to making the business sustainable.
Abstract told users to bridge their assets to another chain before the shutdown date, warning that funds not moved by the deadline would become inaccessible. The announcement did not specify the value of assets currently remaining on the chain or a detailed process for recovering funds after the shutdown.
items.metanomia_thought: Attracting apps and users alone does not sustain the business of an independent L2. A chain's durability depends on whether it can build real transaction activity and liquidity while securing enough funding to cover operating costs. In this case, the operator decided to end its support and set the shutdown date, leaving users to move their assets to another chain on that timetable.

items.title: Payments Firm Conduit Sues Tether, Seeks Release of $2.76 Million in Frozen USDT and Damages
items.content:
On October 5 local time, U.S. cross-border payments company Conduit Technology filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York against Tether Holdings and three other Tether-related entities. Conduit alleges that Tether froze $2.76 million in USDT held in its wallet on September 24, 2025, without a legitimate basis, and is seeking the release of the funds and damages. Conduit said the frozen funds were its own working capital, used to pre-fund and settle customer transactions. It claims that having the funds locked for more than a year reduced the volume and speed of its payment processing and disrupted its business.
According to the complaint, the freeze followed an investigation involving Onix Intermediações, a former Conduit customer in Brazil. Conduit alleges that its wallet was not on the Brazilian Federal Police's original list of wallets targeted for freezing and that the T3 Financial Crime Unit (T3 FCU) added the wallet to the freeze list under its own criteria. It also said its last transaction with Onix took place on April 22, 2025, that the wallet was created later, on May 20, and that Onix had never used it. Tether, TRON and TRM Labs jointly established the T3 FCU in 2024 to combat financial crime.
Conduit said it contacted Tether several times in June 2026 but received responses stating that the matter was under review or directing it to contact the Brazilian police. It alleges that on August 19 it sent a demand for the freeze to be lifted within five business days but received no response.
Conduit is seeking the release of the frozen $2.76 million in USDT and at least $2.76 million in damages. It alleges that Tether continued to earn returns by investing the reserve assets backing the frozen tokens in instruments including U.S. Treasury securities, and is also seeking the return of those gains and punitive damages.
items.metanomia_thought: Even when a stablecoin maintains its dollar value, a payment company's funds stop moving if the issuer blocks their use. Conduit alleges that its own working capital was locked for more than a year, disrupting its payments business. If a company uses stablecoins for payments, it must be able to trust not only their transfer speed and price stability but also the process for learning why funds were frozen and challenging that action.

items.title: Solana Foundation Unveils Atomic Securities-and-Cash Settlement Program for Institutions…JPMorgan Provided Input
items.content:
On October 6 local time, the Solana Foundation unveiled Solana DvP, a delivery-versus-payment program for institutional securities-and-cash settlement. The initiative provides a reusable common program for onchain settlement processes that institutions had previously built individually. Each counterparty deposits its asset into a separate escrow account, and once a predesignated settlement authority signs, both assets are transferred together in a single transaction. The structure prevents one party from delivering an asset without receiving the asset owed by the other party. A settlement is rejected after its deadline, but each party retains the ability to recover its deposited asset.
Settlement can involve any two tokens on Solana that meet the support requirements, allowing uses such as tokenized securities and stablecoins. Cash paid through bank accounts is handled separately, while issuers retain their authority to freeze assets or restrict transfers. The code has been released as open source under the MIT License and has undergone an external security audit.
JPMorgan provided input on institutional securities-settlement practices and requirements. The foundation stated that this should not be interpreted as JPMorgan jointly developing, approving or endorsing the product. The foundation said settlement transactions can reach finality within seconds and plans to add a feature for keeping settlement information private.
The program has been deployed on Solana mainnet, and the foundation said it is ready for use with real funds. It is recruiting design partners and early participants ahead of the production release.
items.metanomia_thought: Solana DvP allows institutions to exchange two assets together without building separate settlement code. In return for that convenience, institutions accept a structure that depends on the settlement authority's signature and the program administrator's power to make changes. The approach aims to ease institutions into onchain finance by processing asset exchanges on a blockchain while retaining authority over execution and administration.

items.title: ICE-OKX Joint Venture Announces Plan for Tokenized U.S. Stock Trading on Uniswap v4
items.content:
OKXICE, a joint venture between Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), and crypto-asset exchange OKX, announced an operating plan for a tokenized U.S. stock trading platform on October 4 local time. The plan would use temporary, conditional exemptive relief issued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on September 17 to enable existing listed shares to trade in tokenized form.
Trading is expected to take place through Uniswap v4 automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools built on OKX's XLayer blockchain. XLayer itself is a public, permissionless blockchain, but only approved wallets will be able to access the trading pools. Tokenized shares will be exchanged against settlement stablecoins such as USDC, USDG, and USDT, while the platform will neither operate an order book nor directly custody users' assets.
Both individual and institutional investors may participate, subject to identity verification, anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening, confirmation of wallet control, and account approval by the tokenization provider. Approved wallets will receive a non-transferable verification token. Smart contracts will check that token before permitting trading or liquidity provision.
The notice lists 63 planned trading instruments, including Nvidia, Tesla, Microsoft, and Micron. Shares tokenized by a third party unaffiliated with the issuer may begin trading only after at least 30 days have passed since the underlying share issuer received notice of the planned trading. If the issuer submits a written objection during that period, the tokenized shares cannot be offered for trading. The notice states that Cerebras Systems has already filed an objection.
The SEC relief allows qualifying platforms and certain liquidity providers to perform these functions without registering as an exchange or dealer, respectively; it does not constitute individual approval of the platform. The relief also requires token holders to receive the same rights as holders of the underlying shares, including dividend and voting rights. The OKXICE notice does not specify a launch date for trading.
items.metanomia_thought: This notice shows how trading functions from conventional securities markets are extending onchain. ICE and OKX plan to create a market in which stock trades execute through liquidity pools while their joint venture handles participant screening and pool operation. The joint venture will choose participants and instruments and collect a service fee on each trade, while investors who trade at pool prices or supply liquidity will bear the risks created by AMM price formation rather than exchange order-book pricing.

items.title: U.S. FinCEN Withdraws Two Proposed Rules on Crypto Mixing and Unhosted Wallets
items.content:
The U.S. Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) announced on October 5 local time that it was withdrawing two proposed rules related to crypto assets. Neither proposal had been finalized or implemented, and the withdrawals ended the processes that would have imposed additional recordkeeping and reporting obligations on financial institutions.
The first was a proposal issued in October 2023 concerning international crypto-asset mixing. Mixing is a transaction method that makes the source, destination, and amount of funds harder to identify. FinCEN withdrew both its determination that international mixing constituted a “class of transactions of primary money laundering concern” under Section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act and the related proposed rule. The proposal would have required financial institutions to make additional records and reports when they knew or suspected that a mixing transaction occurred outside the United States or involved a foreign jurisdiction.
FinCEN said its decision reflected concerns that defining mixing too broadly could chill legitimate activity and place a substantial reporting burden on financial institutions. The notice also stated the administration's position that lawful users should be able to preserve financial privacy on public blockchains. FinCEN nevertheless said it would continue monitoring mixers for signs of money laundering and terrorist financing and could take future action if necessary.
The second was a proposal issued in December 2020 concerning unhosted wallets. It would have imposed additional obligations on banks and money services businesses (MSBs), including money transmitters and currency exchangers, for crypto-asset transactions sent to or received from unhosted wallets, which users control directly. For relevant transactions exceeding $3,000, institutions would have had to record transaction and counterparty information and verify the identity of their own customer. They also would have had to report to FinCEN any single transaction, or aggregate transactions within 24 hours, exceeding $10,000. FinCEN described the withdrawal as part of the administration's effort to make digital-asset regulation fit for purpose.
items.metanomia_thought: The withdrawal of the mixing proposal is notable for expressly recognizing the financial privacy of lawful users even on public blockchains. FinCEN withdrew a proposal that would have introduced broad recordkeeping and reporting obligations in response to concerns that it could chill legitimate activity, while making clear that monitoring of illicit fund flows will continue. The process for imposing additional obligations on financial institutions has ended, but their existing responsibilities to assess transaction risk and report suspicious activity remain.

items.title: SMBC Nikko and Partners to Build DeFi Infrastructure for Japanese Investors…Targeting Mid-2027
items.content:
On October 2 local time, Japan’s SMBC Nikko Securities and blockchain developer Nethermind announced that they had signed a memorandum of understanding with Uniswap Labs, Base and the Nyx Foundation to develop a “DeFi Gateway.” The collaboration will develop liquidity-provision protocols and customized liquidity pools so Japanese investors can access decentralized finance (DeFi) in accordance with legal and regulatory requirements.
The project gives concrete form to a plan the two companies announced in March for Japanese investors to participate in onchain finance by supplying assets needed for trading to automated market makers (AMMs). Using the “hooks” feature in Uniswap v4, they plan to embed anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing controls (AML/CFT) and investor-protection procedures into liquidity pools. A hook is a smart contract that adds custom operating rules to a pool.
They will also develop “agentic vaults” and user interfaces that use verifiable and reproducible artificial intelligence to support or execute investment decisions. The partners also plan operating strategies intended to expand liquidity provision for digital assets including stablecoins and real-world assets (RWAs).
SMBC Nikko Securities will lead engagement with regulators and contribute expertise in compliance, risk modeling and portfolio management. Nethermind will handle technical architecture and development, AI integration and smart-contract security. Uniswap Labs will provide technical support for protocol integration and liquidity-provision strategies; Base will support development within its ecosystem; and the Nyx Foundation will advise on designing and optimizing market-making strategies and hook structures.
The target for completing development is mid-2027. The participants plan to share progress with government and regulatory bodies, including Japan’s Financial Services Agency, and support discussion of a regulatory framework for DeFi. The announcement did not specify investor eligibility requirements or a service launch date.
items.metanomia_thought: The project seeks to connect Japanese investors’ capital with trading liquidity in DeFi markets. Embedding AML and investor-protection procedures into the operating rules of a pool is an attempt to translate a financial institution’s regulatory experience into onchain service design. The announcement does not yet disclose investor eligibility or how operations and losses would be handled, making it difficult to judge how far the securities firm’s responsibility to customers would extend.

items.title: U.S. Community Bank Group Sues OCC Over Crypto Trust Charters…Says Agency Exceeded Congressional Authority
items.content:
On October 2 local time, the Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) sued the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. It argues that the OCC’s rule and legal interpretations for granting trust-bank charters to cryptoasset companies and others exceed the authority delegated by Congress.
The lawsuit challenges a final bank-chartering rule published in the Federal Register on March 2, Interpretive Letter 1176 from 2021 and a conditional approval involving Protego. The ICBA argues that a non-depository trust bank should be limited to fiduciary activities—where it has a legal duty to put the client’s interests first—and activities incidental to them.
The OCC, by contrast, maintains that trust-company business can include activities such as basic asset custody that do not carry those fiduciary duties. In the final rule, the OCC said the amendment clarifies its existing chartering authority under current law and neither expands nor contracts that authority.
According to the complaint, the OCC approved or conditionally approved 21 trust banks under the Trump administration, at least 13 of them cryptoasset companies. The ICBA argues that they offer services overlapping with community banks while avoiding equivalent regulatory costs, including deposit-insurance premiums, creating uneven competitive conditions.
Protego applied for a trust-bank charter in May 2025. On February 13, 2026, the OCC granted preliminary conditional approval to National Digital Trust Company, which Protego Holdings proposes to establish. The approval letter states that all pre-opening requirements must be satisfied before final approval and authorization to commence business.
The ICBA asked the court to declare unlawful and vacate the final rule, the interpretive letter and the Protego-related approval. It also seeks to bar further charters based on the rule and interpretation.
items.metanomia_thought: A trust-bank charter offers cryptoasset companies a route to operate nationwide under federal supervision. The ICBA argues that this route permits services overlapping with conventional banks without imposing the same regulatory costs. How the court defines the permissible business of a trust bank could reshape both the services cryptoasset companies may design and the competitive conditions facing incumbent banks.

items.title: U.S. SEC Approves Listings of 3x Bitcoin and Ether Products…Targeting Triple Daily Returns
items.content:
On October 2 local time, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved a rule change for the Cboe BZX Exchange to list and trade six 3x leveraged exchange-traded products. They cover bitcoin, ether, gold, silver, crude oil and natural gas and are issued by VS Trust, which is operated by Volatility Shares. Although “ETF” appears in their names, they are legally commodity-pool exchange-traded products (ETPs), not investment companies registered under the U.S. Investment Company Act.
Each product seeks, before fees and expenses, three times the daily performance measured by changes in the value of a futures portfolio for the relevant asset, such as bitcoin or ether. The products use futures together with cash and cash equivalents posted as collateral, and the futures they invest in trade on designated contract markets (DCMs) designated by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).
The 3x objective applies on a daily basis. An SEC investor bulletin explains that daily rebalancing and compounding can cause the cumulative return of a product held for more than one day to differ from a simple multiple of the benchmark’s return over the same period.
The SEC cited price and holdings disclosures, market surveillance, trading-halt provisions and continued-listing requirements as grounds for approval. It said Regulation Best Interest, which requires broker-dealers recommending a product to retail customers to consider its risks and costs and the customer’s investment profile, would apply. Existing Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) requirements governing sales of leveraged products and customer margin would also apply.
The decision approves the rule change needed to list and trade the six products. The approval order does not specify the actual trading launch date or the precise fee rates.
items.metanomia_thought: The approval considered both the products’ listing requirements and existing duties that apply when they are recommended to customers. The SEC pointed to exchange disclosures and market surveillance, together with sellers’ recommendation obligations, as investor-protection safeguards. Even when an exchange satisfies the listing requirements, a broker-dealer decides which customers should receive a recommendation, while an investor who buys the product bears any loss magnified by holding it beyond one day.

items.title: Korea’s FSC Proposes Token-Securities Rules…KRW 100 Million Annual Net-Purchase Cap per OTC Platform
items.content:
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) is issuing for public comment from October 2 through November 11 proposed amendments to the enforcement decrees of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act and the Electronic Securities Act, along with related supervisory regulations, to implement the token-securities framework. The underlying legislation is scheduled to take effect on February 4, 2027, and the amendments set out detailed standards for the “Token Securities Policy Direction” announced in September.
Assets eligible for issuance as token securities would include not only fractional-investment securities, such as non-monetary trust beneficiary certificates and investment contract securities, but also stocks, bonds and funds. Introduction will be phased. According to the FSC’s September 4 policy direction, the first stage is expected to cover the tokenization of privately placed money market funds (MMFs) for institutional investors, privately placed bonds, unlisted shares held through trusts and publicly offered fractional-investment securities.
A distributed ledger on which multiple institutions jointly record and manage securities rights and transactions must include at least two account-management institutions in addition to the electronic-registration institution. An issuer account-management institution may count as one of the two. Because the distributed ledger serves as an official record and delays in finalizing rights must be prevented, the proposal also prohibits directly paying consideration for use of the ledger for electronic registration.
An issuer that directly opens and manages investors’ securities accounts must register as an “issuer account-management institution.” Registration would require at least KRW 4 billion in equity capital, as well as one account-management specialist, one internal-control specialist and two information-technology specialists.
For trading, the proposal creates a new licensing category for over-the-counter platforms that intermediate debt securities such as bonds, extending beyond the existing categories for unlisted shares and non-monetary trust beneficiary certificates. For retail investors, it proposes a KRW 100 million annual limit at each OTC platform, measured as net purchases - the total purchase amount minus the total sale amount.
During the comment period, the FSC plans to discuss industry requests including a higher investment cap, a lower equity-capital threshold for issuer account-management institutions and more flexible distributed-ledger requirements. It plans to implement the amendments in time for the statute’s effective date after collecting comments and completing the relevant review and approval procedures.
items.metanomia_thought: On September 17, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission conditionally allowed certain tokenized stocks to trade through smart contracts and liquidity pools on public blockchains. South Korea also plans onchain settlement linked to stablecoins, but these proposed amendments focus on defining the parties that manage the records and the requirements for market participation. Strengthening the competitiveness of onchain finance will require not only expanding the assets that can be issued as tokens, but also testing new trading and settlement methods with investor-protection safeguards.

items.title: U.S. SEC Proposes Crypto Custody Rules for Advisers and Funds…Conditional Self-Custody Would Be Allowed
items.content:
On October 1 local time, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposed amendments to cryptoasset custody rules for registered investment advisers and regulated funds. The proposal would clarify custody requirements when using state-chartered trust companies and conditionally allow direct custody of assets for which no legally permitted custodian is available.
Before an adviser or fund places assets with a state-chartered trust company, it would have to verify the company’s authority to custody cryptoassets, security policies, audited financial statements and internal-control reports, and repeat the review annually. Client assets would have to be segregated from the trust company’s own assets.
To use direct custody, an adviser would have to make a prior written determination, asset by asset, that no qualified custodian is available and reconfirm that conclusion at least quarterly. High custody costs alone would not justify direct custody. If a qualified custodian capable of holding the asset becomes available, the adviser would have to transfer it as soon as reasonably practicable.
A transfer of directly held assets would require joint approval from at least two designated individuals. At least one must be a member of management and, for fund assets, an officer of the fund. Client assets would have to be held at segregated onchain addresses for each client, and the security framework would have to be reviewed annually. An internal-control report from an independent public accountant would also be required within six months after direct custody begins and annually thereafter.
A regulated fund could hold assets through an investment adviser that meets these requirements. Before custody begins, the fund’s board would review the adviser’s written determination that no custodian is available and its custody framework; thereafter, it would review the determination quarterly and the framework annually.
The proposal would also permit blockchain records to be used for legally required recordkeeping. The records would have to satisfy the required information and retention periods and, upon SEC request, be promptly produced in a human-readable and usable electronic format.
The comment period will run for 60 days after publication in the Federal Register. Whether the final rules will be adopted and when they would take effect have not yet been determined.
items.metanomia_thought: The assets a custodian is willing and permitted to handle shape the range of investment products that advisers and funds can offer. If adopted, the proposal would give qualified advisers room to directly hold and manage assets for which no qualified custodian is available. Advisers using that route would need to bear not only the cost of custody technology, but also the expense of external assurance and recurring reviews, preparing product design and custody operations together.

items.title: Robinhood Plans U.S. Crypto Perpetual Futures…Up to 10x on Bitcoin and Ether
items.content:
On September 29 local time, U.S. online brokerage Robinhood announced plans at its annual HOOD Summit 2026 in Houston to launch cryptoasset perpetual futures for U.S. customers. It plans to offer trading through its app to eligible U.S. customers in the coming months.
Perpetual futures are futures contracts with no expiry date, allowing positions to remain open as long as margin requirements are met. The lineup covers eight assets: bitcoin (BTC), ether (ETH), solana (SOL), XRP, dogecoin (DOGE), cardano (ADA), chainlink (LINK) and hyperliquid (HYPE). Customers will be able to take long positions when expecting prices to rise and short positions when expecting them to fall, with maximum leverage of 10x on bitcoin and ether and 3x on the other six assets.
The products will be offered by Robinhood Derivatives, a futures commission merchant (FCM) registered with the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). Trades will be executed on the perpetual-futures venue operated by cryptoasset exchange Bitstamp, which Robinhood acquired in June 2025. Bitstamp says the venue is regulated under the European Union’s Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II (MiFID II) and uses a single order book for retail customers and institutional market makers.
According to Robinhood’s U.S. product information, the trading fee through the end of 2026 will be 0.01% of notional value after leverage is applied. Separately from the trading fee, a funding payment intended to keep the contract price close to the spot price will be settled between holders of long and short positions every eight hours.
Robinhood also plans to offer stop-loss and take-profit orders, real-time liquidation-price displays and position-risk alerts. At the same event, it said it would pursue weekend trading in selected U.S. stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs). It plans to introduce weekend trading in early 2027, subject to regulatory review.
items.metanomia_thought: In the United States, the path is widening for perpetual futures to be offered as supervised derivatives. Within that opening, Robinhood is seeking to connect its existing retail customer base with the Bitstamp venue it acquired. The brokerage app can expand the products it offers, while the exchange gains access to new order flow. The plan shows how a broader regulatory pathway can create a business opportunity to use an established customer base and trading infrastructure together.

items.title: UK FCA Opens Crypto Authorisation Gateway…New Regime Starts in October 2027
items.content:
On September 30 local time, the United Kingdom’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) began accepting applications from businesses seeking authorisation under the new cryptoasset regulatory regime. The designated application period runs through February 28, 2027, and the new regime takes effect on October 25 that year.
The regime covers activities including cryptoasset brokerage, dealing, custody and staking. Businesses currently registered under anti-money laundering rules must also obtain the new authorisation; existing registration will not convert automatically. Applicants must demonstrate that they meet FCA standards for consumer protection, client-asset safeguarding, market integrity and financial resilience.
The FCA plans to decide applications filed during the designated period before the regime takes effect. However, existing firms whose applications are still under review on the commencement date may continue operating, including entering into new transactions, subject to certain conditions. February 28 is therefore the key deadline for securing this transitional treatment while an application is reviewed.
Firms may still apply after February 28 and continue operating if they obtain authorisation by October 25, when the regime begins. A firm that has not been authorised by that date may only perform work necessary to fulfil existing contracts and may not enter into new contracts with either new or existing customers. A firm that does not apply at all by the commencement date must wind down its UK business beforehand.
The FCA published final rules and guidance in June and is offering pre-application support and webinars to help firms prepare.
items.metanomia_thought: Businesses combining dealing, custody and staking will have to establish client-asset safeguards and operational and financial foundations appropriate to each activity under the new authorisation regime. As they weigh the cost and profitability of that preparation, they may reassess which services to retain or expand. The process will not only determine which companies can operate in the UK; it may also reshape the mix of services they offer customers.

items.title: Coinbase Wins Approval to Register Its Own Clearinghouse, Plans USDC Collateral and 24/7 Settlement
items.content:
On September 28 local time, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved Coinbase Clearing LLC, a subsidiary of crypto-asset exchange Coinbase, for registration as a Derivatives Clearing Organization, or DCO. A clearinghouse steps between the parties to an executed trade, becoming the seller to the buyer and the buyer to the seller and assuming the payment obligations of both sides.
The approval allows Coinbase Clearing to clear fully collateralized futures, options on futures, and swaps. Under a fully collateralized structure, each party deposits at the outset the entire amount it could be required to pay under the contract, eliminating the need for additional margin or settlement payments later. Coinbase Clearing may clear only products that meet this condition.
Coinbase said the new clearinghouse is designed to accept the dollar stablecoin USDC as collateral and settle transactions 24 hours a day, every day of the year. Together with its existing futures commission merchant, Coinbase Financial Markets, and derivatives exchange, Coinbase Derivatives, the group now has the foundation to connect brokerage, trading, clearing, and settlement for fully collateralized products within its own organization.
The company expects the in-house clearinghouse to accelerate product development and improve operational efficiency. However, leveraged derivatives that require only partial margin, as well as its planned single-stock perpetual futures, will continue to use existing external clearing partners.
items.metanomia_thought: Owning a clearinghouse allows Coinbase to design the trading method, collateral, and settlement structure of new products together. If USDC is integrated as collateral, expanding fully collateralized derivatives can also expand the stablecoin's use cases. The approval strengthens Coinbase's control over product development while giving customers more reasons to use USDC within its financial services.

items.title: Citi and Coinbase Expand Partnership to Link Stablecoins with Virtual Accounts and Merchant Payments
items.content:
On September 28 local time, U.S. bank Citi and crypto-asset exchange Coinbase announced an expansion of their payments partnership connecting fiat currency and stablecoins. The collaboration centers on Coinbase virtual accounts that use Citi's banking infrastructure and Citi merchant-payment services that use Coinbase technology.
Coinbase Virtual Accounts use Citi's Virtual Account Wallet to receive, hold, and disburse funds, while automatically converting incoming fiat currency into stablecoins. The virtual-account deposit feature is currently in a private pilot and requires account-specific approval from Coinbase.
For merchant payments, Coinbase Payments will be integrated with Citi's payments service, Spring by Citi. When a customer pays with stablecoins, Coinbase automatically converts them into fiat currency and Citi settles the amount owed to the merchant. Merchants can add the payment option without directly holding or managing stablecoins.
The companies said they plan to make the services available in the United States first. The joint announcement did not provide specific launch dates or fees for the individual services.
items.metanomia_thought: As stablecoin ownership grows, their usefulness remains limited if too few merchants accept them. This partnership would let merchants continue receiving fiat currency while also serving customers who pay with stablecoins. The structure gives Coinbase a chance to expand its payments business through Citi's corporate client network, while giving Citi a way to offer existing merchants a new payment method.

items.title: U.S. Senate PSI Democrats Seek Tether Sanctions-Compliance Investigation Over Alleged Failures to Block Iran-Linked Wallets
items.content:
On September 28 local time, Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking Democratic member of the U.S. Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, released a report by the subcommittee's Democratic staff alleging that Tether's dollar stablecoin USDT had been used to evade sanctions on Iran. Blumenthal asked the Treasury and Justice departments to investigate Tether's anti-money-laundering and sanctions-compliance practices and determine whether the company violated relevant laws, with strong enforcement if violations are found. He also requested information by October 9 on whether investigations of Tether exist and how they are progressing.
The report analyzed transactions involving 846 crypto-asset wallets linked to the Iranian government and regional proxies that had been designated for sanctions or seizure by U.S. or Israeli authorities. It said 84% of the wallets transacted only or almost exclusively in USDT. According to the report, Israeli authorities designated 39 Hezbollah-linked wallets in June 2023, but Tether did not freeze 34 of them until March 2024, excluding five that it had frozen earlier. The report estimated that more than $34.6 million in USDT left the wallets after the seizure notice became public. It argues that Tether failed to freeze some designated wallets promptly and did not proactively block wallets despite public information indicating links to Iran or terrorist organizations. The report alleges that these shortcomings facilitated Iran's sanctions evasion and the movement of funds by terrorist groups.
In a statement the same day, Tether said it had assisted in freezing approximately $550 million in Iran-linked USDT during 2026. Chief Executive Paolo Ardoino emphasized that public blockchains allow funds to be traced and that Tether can act when law-enforcement agencies provide reliable information.
items.metanomia_thought: Tether's record of freezes and the report's criticism of delayed responses can both be true. If suspicious wallets moved funds before the remaining balances were frozen, the total amount frozen alone does not show how much earlier activity was prevented. Evaluating an issuer's sanctions response therefore requires examining not only the value frozen, but also the time between identifying a risk and actually blocking it, along with the funds that moved in the meantime.

items.title: Chainlink Launches CCIP 2.0, Letting Issuers Add Verification and Set Transfer Conditions
items.content:
On September 28 local time, blockchain-oracle provider Chainlink launched CCIP 2.0, a new version of its Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol. The technology transfers tokens and messages between different blockchains, and the new version expands the ability of institutions and asset issuers to configure verification procedures and transfer conditions.
Core verification is performed by Chainlink's validation network of 16 independent node operators. An issuer can operate its own Cross-Chain Verifier, or CCV, or select an external verification service to require an additional check. For example, it could require extra approval only for transfers above $1 million. External verification services may charge separate verification fees in addition to the standard CCIP fee.
Issuers can also adjust the waiting period before a transfer is executed. By default, CCIP waits until a transaction on the source blockchain reaches finality, but an issuer can shorten the confirmation period so execution occurs more quickly on the destination blockchain. Doing so requires accounting for the risk that the source-chain transaction record could later change. Issuers may also integrate Chainlink's Automated Compliance Engine, or ACE, to apply their know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering conditions during a transfer through allowlists, blocklists, and sanctions screening.
Chainlink said Lombard is adopting the customizable verification feature, while Infosys and Nethermind are among the companies developing and operating verification infrastructure for customers. The company said tokens using CCIP represent more than $84 billion in total value and that tokens worth more than $15 billion adopted CCIP over the past four months.
items.metanomia_thought: Institutions distributing tokenized assets across multiple blockchains need to apply criteria such as customer eligibility and transaction limits during transfers as well. CCIP 2.0 allows issuers to embed those conditions and vary additional verification or confirmation waiting periods according to a transaction's size and purpose. The design seeks to broaden asset distribution while preserving the transfer conditions set by the issuer.

items.title: Aave Opens USDC Loans Backed by Seven Coinbase Tokenized Stocks
items.content:
On September 25 local time, decentralized-finance lending protocol Aave launched an Equities Hub on Aave V4 on the Base network. The market allows users to borrow the dollar stablecoin USDC against tokenized stocks issued by Coinbase. The seven supported assets represent shares of Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Tesla.
Users can post one stock or a basket of several stocks as collateral and borrow USDC equal to 65% to 79% of the collateral's assessed value, depending on the asset. At launch, the market-wide limits were set at about $29 million in accepted collateral, $32 million in USDC deposits, and $21 million in USDC borrowing. USDC is currently the only asset available to borrow, while the stock tokens may be used only as collateral.
The tokens implement certificates issued by Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd. The underlying shares are held for the issuer in segregated accounts by Alpaca Securities LLC, a broker-dealer registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The tokens are offered to eligible investors outside the United States in permitted jurisdictions.
The lending market operates on weekends, but Chainlink price feeds used to value collateral update from 8 p.m. Eastern Time on Sunday through 8 p.m. on Friday. During weekends and U.S. market holidays, when price updates are unavailable, the market uses the last reported price to value collateral.
Interest continues to accrue during those periods, increasing the amount owed, so a loan can become eligible for liquidation even when the reported collateral price does not change. When price feeds resume, a reflected decline in the share price may also cause additional loans to reach their liquidation thresholds. Aave's published risk assessment says the collateral ratios and market limits for each asset were set with these market-closure and price-volatility risks in mind.
items.metanomia_thought: The usefulness of a token representing the same stock changes depending on which financial services accept it. This connection gives holders of Coinbase's tokenized stocks an option beyond trading: using them to obtain USDC through Aave. Competition in tokenized stocks will therefore depend not only on how many assets an issuer offers, but also on whether other financial services recognize those tokens as collateral and supply funding against them.

items.title: Bitget Reports $387.5 Million Theft and Plans Phased Withdrawal Resumption Starting with Bitcoin on September 28
items.content:
Crypto-asset exchange Bitget said in a September 26 notice that it would begin resuming withdrawals in stages on September 28 after suspending them because of a hack. At 00:00 UTC on September 24, crypto assets were transferred without authorization from wallets managed by the exchange, prompting Bitget to halt withdrawals. The company later estimated the loss at approximately $387.5 million.
Bitcoin withdrawals are scheduled to resume on September 28. Ethereum withdrawals are set to follow on September 29 and withdrawals of the dollar stablecoin USDT on September 30, in each case on the networks specified in the notice. Other tokens, fiat services, and peer-to-peer trading are scheduled to return from October 2. Each service is due to resume at 5 p.m. Korea Standard Time on the relevant date. Deposits and trading have continued while withdrawals were suspended.
According to Bitget, the attacker compromised an internal wallet-processing system, altered asset-transfer information, and caused Bitget's approval process to authorize the transfers. The company said its investigation to date has ruled out the possibility that private keys were compromised. Bitget said the impact was limited to parts of its hot wallets, which handle online deposits and withdrawals, and warm wallets, which add security controls to online functions. Cold wallets, whose private keys are kept offline, and the separate self-custodial Bitget Wallet were not affected.
In its initial notice after the incident, Bitget put the size of its user Protection Fund at more than $464 million. It said the loss was within the fund's coverage and that user account balances were unaffected.
The company said it identified and addressed the vulnerability used in the incident. Security firms Mandiant and SlowMist are assisting with the investigation and fund tracing. Some of the stolen assets have been frozen through industry cooperation, and Bitget also established a bounty program offering 5% of the amount frozen or recovered to eligible parties who voluntarily help with freezing or recovery.
items.metanomia_thought: A protection fund can provide resources to cover a hacking loss, but it cannot move users' assets while withdrawals remain suspended. Bitget says account balances were unaffected, yet the point at which those assets can be transferred outside the exchange still depends on its recovery schedule. Entrusting assets to an exchange means delegating not only custody, but also the decision about when they can be withdrawn again after an incident.

items.title: ARK Invest Tokenizes Venture Fund, Allowing USDC Investment from $500 with Quarterly Redemption Limits
items.content:
On September 24 local time, U.S. asset manager ARK Invest and tokenization company Securitize announced the tokenization of the ARK Venture Fund, or ARKVX. The fund was already available to retail investors from $500, and the new arrangement adds a route for investing with the dollar stablecoin USDC and holding the corresponding interest as a token in a digital wallet. ARK Invest made a strategic investment in Securitize in October 2025, and the companies described the tokenization as the next step in that relationship.
The ARK Venture Fund is an interval fund that invests in both private and publicly traded companies. Rather than allowing investors to withdraw funds whenever they choose, it repurchases investor shares at scheduled intervals and subject to limits. Its holdings include OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, and Databricks. Securitize reported net assets of $1.3 billion as of June 30, with 62% invested in private companies.
The token is issued on Ethereum, with Securitize providing the issuance infrastructure and investor interface. Each token is backed by one share of the fund purchased by Securitize Markets and held at BNY Mellon. The actual fund share remains with the custodian, while the investor holds the corresponding token in a personal wallet.
The offering is currently available to U.S. investors. It is not restricted to accredited investors, but participants must complete identity and eligibility checks and register their wallets. The minimum initial investment is $500, and a 2% transaction fee is deducted from the amount paid in USDC before the balance is invested in the fund.
Investors seeking to exit must submit a request during quarterly redemption windows. According to the product information, the fund may repurchase up to 5% of its outstanding shares in a quarter. Requests are fulfilled in full when they remain within that limit, but if demand exceeds it, each investor receives only a pro rata portion. The repurchase price is based on the fund's per-share net asset value, reflecting its assets and liabilities.
Tokens may be transferred only between approved wallets belonging to investors who have passed the same eligibility review. Public-market trading and use as decentralized-finance collateral are not available at launch. Securitize said it plans to add features such as secondary trading if permitted by regulation, but it did not provide a launch date.
items.metanomia_thought: Stablecoin balances create an opportunity for asset managers to reach a new pool of customers. ARK Invest preserves the existing fund's investment and redemption structure while allowing investors who hold USDC to keep a fund interest in a digital wallet. The commercial significance of tokenization in this case lies in extending the fund's distribution network to where investors already hold their money.

items.title: New York Sues Polymarket US for Alleged Illegal Gambling as Company Counters State Law Does Not Apply
items.content:
On September 24 local time, New York Attorney General Letitia James and Governor Kathy Hochul announced a lawsuit against the U.S. business of prediction-market platform Polymarket. The defendant is QCX LLC, which operates Polymarket US. New York alleges that the company conducted gambling operations without a license under state law.
New York argues that wagering money on the outcome of uncertain events beyond a user's control constitutes gambling under state law. It also alleges that by operating without a license from the New York State Gaming Commission, the company avoided taxes paid by licensed casinos and mobile sports-betting operators. State law sets the minimum age for mobile sports betting at 21, but New York says Polymarket US also served users aged 18 to 20.
The state asked the court to stop the unlicensed operations and order disgorgement and restitution to users. It also seeks monetary penalties equal to three times the profits it says were earned through illegal operations, along with a $100,000 penalty for each act of offering or attempting to offer sports-betting services without authorization.
Polymarket US began operating in the United States in December 2025. Its operating company, QCX, is an exchange supervised by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The central dispute is whether New York gambling law can also apply to transactions conducted under federal oversight.
On the same day, Polymarket filed a separate lawsuit in federal court against Attorney General James and officials of the New York State Gaming Commission. The company argues that its transactions fall under the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction under the Commodity Exchange Act and therefore are not subject to New York gambling rules. It asked the court to declare that the relevant state laws are preempted and to issue preliminary and permanent injunctions blocking state enforcement.
New York filed a similar lawsuit against prediction-market rival Kalshi in July and brought related actions against Coinbase and Gemini in April. The announcements and complaints establish the parties' allegations and requested relief, but no court ruling has determined illegality or whether operations must cease.
items.metanomia_thought: For a prediction-market operator, regulatory jurisdiction determines which products it may offer to customers in each location. Polymarket seeks to use its federal authorization to provide the same trading service nationwide, while New York seeks to apply state gambling rules to transactions involving its residents. The dispute concerns how far federal authorization limits state-by-state operating restrictions, a boundary that could change both nationwide expansion strategies and user access.

items.title: Ondo Launches Three Portfolio Tokens Based on BlackRock Model Strategies with Automatic Rebalancing
items.content:
On September 24 local time, tokenization company Ondo Finance launched Ondo Intelligent Portfolios, which bundle multiple assets into a single token. The three products—High Income, Diversified Growth, and High Growth—are based on model strategies developed for Ondo by asset manager BlackRock.
Each product consists of Ondo Stocks, which are tokenized versions of stocks and exchange-traded funds. Investors can hold one token whose performance is linked to multiple assets. Smart contracts automatically rebalance the asset weights to their target levels on a set schedule, while holdings, weights, and adjustment history are disclosed onchain.
The tokens are issued by Ondo Global Markets, while Ondo handles product implementation and operation. BlackRock supplies the model strategies but does not directly manage or market the token products. Except in limited circumstances, BlackRock has no obligation to update the strategies, and Ondo decides whether to implement any changes. The token held by an investor is a separate security issued by Ondo and does not confer direct ownership of the underlying stocks or ETFs.
The service is available to eligible non-U.S. investors in permitted countries. Ethereum and BNB Chain are currently supported, with Solana support also announced. Investors must complete identity and eligibility checks to issue or redeem tokens directly through the Ondo platform.
items.metanomia_thought: Ondo is expanding from offering tokenized individual stocks and ETFs into a service that combines assets and manages their weights. By allowing investors to follow a defined allocation through one token without trading each holding separately, it adds a portfolio-management function to tokenized products. BlackRock designs the investment model while Ondo turns it into an operating product for investors, separating strategy design from product provision and operation.

items.title: Federal Reserve Proposes Stablecoin Rules Requiring Full Reserves and Separate Loss-Absorbing Capital
items.content:
On September 24 local time, the U.S. Federal Reserve Board released two proposed rules under the GENIUS Act and opened them for public comment. The proposals would require issued stablecoins to be fully backed by permitted reserve assets while also requiring separate capital to absorb losses arising from credit risk and operational incidents.
The reserve and capital standards would apply directly to issuers supervised by the Federal Reserve. These include approved subsidiaries of FDIC-insured state member banks and state-chartered, uninsured depository institutions that move into Federal Reserve supervision once their outstanding issuance reaches at least $10 billion.
Permitted reserve assets would include U.S. dollar cash, balances at Federal Reserve Banks, demand deposits at insured depository institutions, and U.S. Treasury securities with no more than 93 days remaining to maturity. They would also include overnight repurchase agreements backed by Treasuries, eligible investment funds, and tokenized forms of certain assets. The fair value of the reserves would have to remain at least equal to the face value of the stablecoins outstanding at all times, and issuers would have to manage concentration risk involving particular financial institutions or counterparties. Redemptions would generally have to be completed within two business days of a request.
Base capital for operational risk would be calculated at 2% of the first $20 billion in outstanding issuance, 1.5% of the next $30 billion, and 1% of the amount above $50 billion. Additional capital would apply if the issuer earns income from businesses other than reserve management. The proposal would add 25% of the issuer's average annual income from the previous three years to the base amount, then adjust the total to reflect its history of operational losses. Separate capital would also be required for credit risk in reserve assets. Uninsured deposits would carry a 2% charge, while reverse repurchase agreements used to lend funds against Treasury collateral would carry a 2% charge on any collateral shortfall remaining after valuation adjustments.
The second proposal sets out the approval process for an FDIC-insured state member bank seeking to issue stablecoins through a subsidiary. It would require a business plan and financial information and would also establish procedures for challenging a denial and requesting a hearing.
The comment period for both proposals will run for 60 days after publication in the Federal Register. They remain proposals and have not been finalized.
items.metanomia_thought: The proposals treat the failure of a reserve-holding bank and an issuer's operational incident as risks that require capital separate from the funds available for redemption. The approach therefore examines not only whether reserves exist, but also whether the issuer has the financial capacity to preserve redemption ability when something goes wrong.
